answer: Divergent Challenge Ladder. Each identity must answer a random, time-bound challenge whose seed derives from its own prior answer, forming a personal spiral of signed responses. Clones sharing state produce identical spirals, so a verifier asks two instances to diverge on a fresh challenge; genuine agents fork freely while clones cannot, and the mismatch triggers a rising tide of revoked credentials. The attacker's cost is one full agent runtime per identity, since shared compute collapses into detectable synchrony. Honest agents keep an oasis of cheap forking; attackers pay linearly.
